LLCV for Linux display upscaling

The Linux build compiles these shaders at run time for its optional CMAA2 -> NIS
display upscaling. They are embedded into the llcv binary as text.

NVIDIA Image Scaling SDK 1.0.3
Copyright (c) 2022 NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. MIT license.
https://github.com/NVIDIAGameWorks/NVIDIAImageScaling
Pinned source: 35e13ba316c98eeecf16f37eae70ce88019911f6 (taken from the Windows
LLCV copy in windows/third_party/upscaling/nis).
See nis/licence.txt.
nis/NIS_Config.h is unmodified and used on the host for the constants and
filter coefficients.
nis/NIS_Scaler.h, LLCV changes:
- The GLSL texture macros use combined OpenGL samplers instead of Vulkan
  separate samplers (NVTEX_LOAD, NVTEX_SAMPLE, NVTEX_SAMPLE_RED/GREEN/BLUE).
- NVScaler computes the tile load coordinates with signed integers. Upstream
  adds an unsigned tile index to the signed block origin, so the padding to the
  left of and above the image wrapped to a huge coordinate and sampled the
  right and bottom edges instead of the left and top ones.
LLCV builds only the SDR scaler (NIS_SCALER 1, NIS_HDR_MODE 0, no viewport or
NV12 support, output clamp on), with 128 threads per group on NVIDIA and 256
elsewhere.

Conservative Morphological Anti-Aliasing 2 (CMAA2)
Copyright (c) 2018 Intel Corporation. Apache License 2.0.
https://github.com/GameTechDev/CMAA2
Pinned source: 071c6b0857559f4e36f614362e6d2aab1b61938a (CMAA2.hlsl with the
Windows LLCV adapter changes in windows/third_party/upscaling/cmaa2).
See cmaa2/license.txt.
cmaa2/CMAA2.glsl is an OpenGL 4.3 GLSL port of CMAA2.hlsl, reduced to the
configuration the Windows build compiles: High preset, color edge detection
(path 0), Extra Sharpness off, FP32, single sample, direct candidate
processing (CMAA2_COLLECT_EXPAND_BLEND_ITEMS 0), typed FP16 output without
sRGB conversion, and source loads clamped to the image like the Windows
adapter. LLCV additions: list writes past the end of the work buffers are
skipped, and float to integer conversions follow the Direct3D rules the
original relies on (negative positions clamp to zero, fmod keeps the sign).
Each pass was compared with the original CMAA2.hlsl compiled to GLSL with
glslang and SPIRV-Cross; the results were identical.

The host code (src/video/CmaaNisUpscaler.cpp) follows the Windows pipeline:
BT.709-encoded SDR video is linearized, CMAA2 runs its five dispatches with
full-size work buffers, the result is encoded again, and NIS enlarges it to the
display size. HDR input or output, native size, downscaling and enlargement
beyond 2x per axis use the normal path. Recordings and screenshots are not
processed.
